state.misconception_label: Does not understand that 2n represents an even number

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: Which of these shows part of the proof that the sum of two odd numbers is even? I got \( \begin{array}{l}2 n+(2 m+1) \\ =2(n+m)+1\end{array} \) because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: You are on the right track with your algebraic manipulation. However, when adding two odd numbers, the result should be an even number. Remember that 2n represents an even number. Try simplifying the expression \(2(n+m)+1\) further to show that it is indeed an even number.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Okay, I think I get that 2n is an even number, but I'm confused about how \(2(n+m)+1\) can be even if it has that "+1" at the end. Doesn't that make it odd? Can you help me see how that works?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: You are correct that the addition of 1 at the end of \(2(n+m)+1\) may seem to make it odd. However, remember that in this case, the expression \(2(n+m)\) represents an even number since 2 times any integer is even. Therefore, when you add 1 to an even number, the result is still an even number. Keep simplifying to show that the sum of two odd numbers is indeed even.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Okay, I think I see what you're saying. So, if \(2(n+m)\) is even, then adding 1 makes it odd, right? But I guess that means I need to look at how the whole thing works together. Can you explain again why the sum of two odd numbers is even? I'm still a bit confused about that part.
